summary: The team is in execution mode on two fronts: locking in a seven-month SEO/AI-visibility strategy anchored on Asia Star and Intelligent China, and finalising the Knowledge website redesign before launch — while a lingering Outlook lockout is quietly blocking day-to-day work.
summaryDetail: Top priority is the global marketing and visibility push: the strategy is set to lead with Asia Star and Intelligent China (US partner programs like Berkeley, Stanford and Columbia held as secondary, with Berkeley a possible third), and Joseph owes the target areas, focus and prompts plus an analysis of Asia Star participant profiles and CRM hot leads, while the team must brief the Google Ads conversion tracking setup and get the Intelligent China webpage live and driving traffic. The Knowledge website redesign is close to done — the current design stays as the base with Joseph's editorial-style layout folded in, BCI/BSI indices surfaced, and videos dispersed by topic rather than a standalone section — but launch is gated on Joseph sharing the HTML inspiration file, a 30-minute feedback-marking session with Julie and the team lead, and cleanup of remaining issues (publication news, She Innovates design consistency, whiteboard-style framing). Urgent this week: clear the Outlook account lockout that's disrupting the whole team (re-add accounts, update passwords across desktop and mobile, check home devices, and confirm with JSB that the backend is unlocked), and push the Knowledge site fixes to unblock launch. Also on the near horizon: the Women in Leadership Forum logistics (Alan's banners/brochures and booth materials, the on-stage video decision at rehearsal), the MBZUAI article and gifting-moment photo, Ira's updated women's figures, and Julie's final review of Professor Jon Liao's English obituary.
